[[Vantaa]] | capacity = 4,700 | coordinates = {{coord|60|15.726|N|24|50.291|E|type:landmark_region:FI-ES|display=inline,title}} | owntitle = | owner = | chrtitle = | chairman = Markku Hynninen | mgrtitle = | manager = | coach = | league = | season = 2016 | position = [[Veikkausliiga]], 12th (relegation and bankruptcy) | kit_alt1 = | pattern_la1 = _black_stripes_thin1 | pattern_b1 = _nikestripeddiv4rb | pattern_ra1 = _black_stripes_thin1 | leftarm1 = FF0000 | body1 = FF0000 | rightarm1 = FF0000 | shorts1 = 000000 | socks1 = 000000 | pattern_name1 = | pattern_la2 = | pattern_b2 =_nikelegend1920wr | pattern_ra2 = | leftarm2 = FFFFFF | body2 = FFFFFF | rightarm2 = FFFFFF | shorts2 = FF0000 | socks2 = FF0000 | pattern_name2 = }} '''PK-35 Vantaa''' (previously '''Pallokerho-35''' or '''PK-35''') was a Finnish men's [[Association football|football]] team, based in [[Vantaa]]. It last played in the [[Veikkausliiga]], the top-tier men's football league in Finland. The team was based at the [[Myyrmäen jalkapallostadion]] in the [[Myyrmäki]] district of Vantaa at the time of its dissolution, after the 2016 season. The Helsinki-based [[PK-35 (men)|PK-35]] is the club's first team and currently competes in the new second-tier [[Ykkösliiga]], starting in 2024. ==History== PK-35 was founded in [[Vyborg]] in 1935. After the [[Finnish Winter War]] and [[Second World War]], PK-35 was refounded in Helsinki in 1948. When PK-35 was coached by [[Pasi Rautiainen]] in the mid-1990s they were promoted to Finland's top division, the Veikkausliiga. After some economic troubles, the club's top representative team was acquired by [[Hjallis Harkimo]] and renamed [[FC Jokerit]]. The PK-35 club, however, continued with the other teams in lower divisions using its original name. PK-35 was promoted to [[Kakkonen]] in 2001 and to [[Ykkönen]] in 2005. === Move to Vantaa === [[File:Pohjola_stadion.jpg|thumb|The team's home ground was [[Myyrmäen jalkapallostadion|Myyrmäki stadion]]]] After the 2008 season Pallokerho-35 decided to move its men's and [[PK-35 Vantaa (women)|women's first team]]s to the [[commuter town]] of Vantaa, where they played at [[ISS Stadion]] in Myyrmäki. The teams were run by a newly created association and competed with the name PK-35 Vantaa. Pallokerho-35 and its other teams (juniors) stayed in [[Helsinki]] under the association PK-35 ry (main club).{{Cite web|url= http://www.pk-35.fi/1935/files/esitysvantaa.pdf|title= PK-35 Vantaa – uusi jalkapalloseura|access-date= 30 December 2008|publisher= Pallokerho-35|date= 17 December 2008|url-status= dead|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110720191538/http://www.pk-35.fi/1935/files/esitysvantaa.pdf|archive-date= 20 July 2011}} === Bankruptcy === The club suffered serious financial problems in its final years. Sitting at the bottom of the [[2016 Veikkausliiga]], the club were docked six points and manager [[Shefki Kuqi]] left to join [[Inter Turku]].[https://yle.fi/urheilu/3-912593] in [[yle]].fi The club was [[Promotion and relegation|relegated]] at the end of the season but did not apply for a licence to play in the [[2017 Ykkönen]] and ceased operations. The club's name continued, however, as the club that split from the [[PK-35 (men)|PK-35]] organisation when it was renamed FC Jokerit began to play in the [[Helsinki]] area [[Kolmonen]] division (4th
